name: Calculating the Average of Floating-Point Numbers
description: Construct a program that reads a series of non-negative floating-point numbers from the user, sums them up, and calculate their average.\nNote that you need to think what value should the program use to indicate the end of the input.
code:
#Step 1: Define the variables that we need for this program
total = 0
count = 0
#/Step 2: Read the first number that the user enters
text = input("Enter a number: ")
num = float(text)
#Step 3: Process the number that the user has entered, then receive and process the next numbers as long as the user enters a non-negative number; otherwise stop
while num >= 0.0 :
    count += 1
    total += num
    print("The sum so far is", total, ", count =", count)
    text = input("Enter a number: ")
    num = float(text) 
#Step 4: Calculate and print the average of the numbers entered by the user
if count == 0 :
    print("No numbers were entered.")
else :
    average = total / count
print("The average is:", average)

1.content: #Step 1: Define the variables that we need for this program

commentList: We need variable total to maintain a running total, which means the sum of the numbers that the user enters. Note that we need to define num as double because it should store the sum of floating-point numbers that we receive from the user.
We need variable count to count how many numbers the user enters. This is required for calculating the average of the numbers that the user enters.

4.content: #/Step 2: Read the first number that the user enters

commentList: We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the first number. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its float representation because the number could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float().
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value.

7.content: #Step 3: Process the number that the user has entered, then receive and process the next numbers as long as the user enters a non-negative number; otherwise stop

commentList:
We need to process the number that the user has entered and repeat receiving and processing the numbers from the user as long as the user enters a number that is not negative. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input number is not a negative number.

We could test whether the input number is non-negative by testing if the number is greater than or equal to zero.

The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters a number that is greater than or equal to zero. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters a negative number.

We have to count the number of values that are entered because we need it for calculating the average. Therefore, each time that the user enters a number, we need to increment the number of values that user has entered by 1. Note that if the user enters 0, it will not be counted.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 1) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable count) and the result is stored in the variable count. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement count = count + 1.
We need to add the number that the user has entered to the running total. So, each time that the user enters a number, that number needs to be added to and stored back into total.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., value of variable num) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable total) and the result is stored in the variable total. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement total = total + num.

11.content: print("The sum so far is", total, ", count =", count)
commentList: Each time the body of the while loop is repeated, the sum and the number of the values that the user has entered will be printed to the default standard output stream. We do this to see how sum and count are updated after each repeat of the loop. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given strings and value of the variables.

We need to read and process the next number that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the next number. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its float representation because the number could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float().
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value.

14.content: #Step 4: Calculate and print the average of the numbers entered by the user

commentList:
We need the if statement at the end of the program to avoid a divide-by-zero error. This occurs if the user immediately enters a negative number before entering any other number.

To determine if the divide-by-zero error would occur, we need to test if the number of values entered by the user is equal to zero.
If the number of values that the user has entered is equal to zero, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream that no numbers were entered. This text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

If the above if test fails (i.e., when the number of values the the user has entered is different from zero), we could calculate the average by dividing the sum by the number of values entered by the user.

We need to calculate the average by dividing the sum of the values by the number of the values that the user entered. Note that since we want to keep the fractional part of the division result, we need to use the real division by using / operator.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "The average is:" and the value of variable average.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
